description: Ancient Indian spatial design and orientation tradition balancing the five cosmic elements (Pancha Bhoota: Earth, Water, Fire, Air, Space) across the cardinal grid of the Vastu Purusha Mandala.
schools_note: Classical texts (Brihat Samhita, Manasara, Samarangana Sutradhara) agree on core cardinal deities, but modern commercial practitioners debate secondary placements such as north-west kitchen options.

rules.rationale: Governed by Agni (Fire deity); placing fire in water (NE) causes family conflict, while in earth (SW) causes instability.
rules.source: Brihat Samhita, Ch. 53 (Vastu-vidya), Verse 70 & Manasara, Ch. 9

rules.rationale: Governed by Nairutya (Earth/Stability); grounds the primary decision-maker and family head.
rules.source: Samarangana Sutradhara of King Bhoja, Ch. 34, Verse 22

rules.rationale: Governed by Ishanya (Water/Ether/Divine consciousness); receives positive morning solar infrared radiation.
Brahmasthana (central 1/9th of mandala) must remain open, unweighted, and unpunctured to allow cosmic energy circulation.
Eliminative functions in NE corrupt divine energy; in SW drain health and financial grounding.
Auspicous padas (Indra, Jayanta, Mukhya) channel vital prana and early morning sunlight.
Depressions and subterranean water in Ishanya enhance prosperity; in fire or earth sectors cause fire or structural distress.
Heavy overhead mass should ballast the highest, heaviest southwest sector, never the light northeast.
Stairs constitute heavy structural loading that must anchor the southern/western quadrant.
Ascent in clockwise pradakshina movement aligns with earth's rotational spin.
Kitchen prep must never share common walls, doors, or drainage stacks with waste facilities.
rules.source: Common modern consensus derived from Manasara purity ordinances

rules.rationale: Decomposition gas discharge is channeled through Vayu (wind) corner away from living core.
